entry.title: Coin & Stock Monitor 1.1.0
entry.content:
Coin & Stock Monitor

Shows live stock and crypto prices on the left side of the taskbar.

Prices come from a configurable JSON API. The default is the Yahoo Finance chart API, which works without an API key for both stocks (AAPL, VNM.VN) and crypto (BTC-USD, ETH-USD).

Network access

This mod sends HTTPS requests from explorer.exe to the URL set in Price API URL. By default that is query1.finance.yahoo.com. It sends one request per symbol (up to 4) at startup, then once every Refresh interval (default 60 seconds). Each request identifies the mod by name in its User-Agent header. No other data is sent. To stop all requests, disable the mod.

Settings

  • Price API URL - requested once per symbol. {symbol} is replaced with the URL-encoded symbol.
  • Price JSON key - the key whose numeric value is the price in the response. Yahoo Finance uses regularMarketPrice.
  • Symbols - comma-separated list, shown in order. At most 4 symbols, shown 2 per line.
  • Entry prices - comma-separated SYMBOL=PRICE pairs. When a symbol has an entry price, its price and signed percentage change from the entry are shown. The color is the gain color when the price is at or above the entry, and the loss color otherwise.
  • Text alignment - left or right inside the monitor area.
  • Left offset and Monitor width - position and size of the monitor area, in pixels from the left edge of the taskbar.
  • Text color - #RRGGBB for symbols and prices without an entry price. The default is green. Leave empty to follow the taskbar theme.
  • Gain color and Loss color - #RRGGBB colors for prices and percentages compared with entry prices.
  • Refresh interval - seconds between fetches (minimum 15).

Changing any setting reloads the mod.

Example: CoinGecko

  • Price API URL: https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/simple/price?ids={symbol}&vs_currencies=usd
  • Price JSON key: usd
  • Symbols: bitcoin,ethereum (CoinGecko coin ids, not ticker symbols)
  • Entry prices: bitcoin=60000 (use the same ids as Symbols)

Limitations

  • Horizontal taskbar on the primary monitor only.
  • The monitor is placed by pixel offset, so it assumes the Start button is centered. With a left-aligned Start button, the monitor overlaps Start.
  • If the taskbar has many apps or a wide Start area, reduce Monitor width so the monitor does not cover the task list.
  • Pixel values are for 100% display scaling.

entry.title: Virtual Desktop Swipe Taskbar Fix 1.0.5
entry.content:
Virtual Desktop Swipe Taskbar Fix

Restores the missing incoming taskbar bitmap during a touchpad virtual desktop swipe on Windows 11.

The issue

Limitation

While a swipe is held, both previews can show the current desktop's taskbar buttons, instead of reflecting the incoming taskbar's current state. This is because Windows has not yet committed the switch during a swipe gesture, and thumbnails taken at that time inevitably look the same as on the outgoing desktop.

Keyboard switching avoids this because it freezes the outgoing taskbar preview and updates the actual taskbar during the transition, allowing the live incoming preview to show the destination desktop's buttons.

ARM64 is not supported: native methods are resolved through symbols, but internal member offsets are discovered from those methods at initialization. Initialization stops if the required symbols or layout cannot be recognized.

entry.title: Mac Island & Dock 2.0.0
entry.content:
Styles and look

  • "Fixed" style: the pill keeps its room at its edge, so maximized windows stop beside it (also right after Windows starts).
  • Notches for the Fixed style: one in the middle, one at each top corner, or three, with curves from flat to wide and sweeping (0-200%); items are dragged between notches in the settings, each notch takes at most its share of the screen, notifications come out of the notch with the bell, and the notches hide each on its own or together as one line.
  • Colors: "Auto" and inverted colors following Windows' light/dark mode, your own colors (fill, text, icons; a warning when they're hard to read), colors following the app in front, and the island's opacity (#6048).
  • Frosted glass on the bar and on the Fixed style's strip (Windows' blur; it turns Windows' transparency effects on, and back off when it's turned off) (#6048, #6063).
  • Islands on every monitor (optional): each other monitor follows the main island's settings or uses a profile of its own; editing a profile from any island updates every island using it.

Place

  • Minimizing to a line at the bottom and on the sides too, and hiding as its line until the mouse reaches it, after a chosen delay (#6048).
  • Staying clear of the taskbar on any edge, and out of a screenshot selection's way.
  • Place and icons per app: also what's playing's parts, the clock, the distance from the edges, the size and the items' order per app; the list scrolls; only for the Island style (the Fixed style and the bar keep one place for every app).
  • A pill longer than the screen stops short of its edges and the mouse wheel slides along it.

Settings, profiles and backup

  • Settings in tabs: General (profiles, backup, place), Look (style and notches, colors, size and transparency, animations), Pill (the items' order, system, desktop, apps and tools, the control center's buttons), Tray, media and clock, Notifications, and Monitors with two or more screens. Wider columns, each option right under the one it depends on, names shown whole on their lines with the selectors and sliders under them; a search through every tab; in the middle of the screen with the bar style; a gear at the bottom of the control center opens them; a dimmed option says why under the mouse.
  • Monitors tab: a map following the real display layout; one screen, all screens, or following the mouse; each other monitor picks the main island's settings or a profile with a click, and opens its own settings from its gear; only the main island shows the notifications.
  • Text boxes work like Windows' (mouse and Shift selection, double click on a word, Ctrl+A); scroll bars easier to see.
  • Profiles: save the settings as profiles (up to 10), rename, delete; the one in use saves every change by itself; an optional pill button switches them (Shift + wheel picks one). The pinned tray icons and their places are kept in them too.
  • Backup: export and import a file with notes, tasks, keyboard shortcuts, calendar events and agendas (their links too, so it's kept private), pinned folders, the tray icons' order and places, the wallpapers' folder, profiles and every island setting.

Pill and items

  • The clock kept in the middle (the other items move around it, no blank part beside it) (#6102), 24 or 12 hours with a small AM/PM, the date order and the month as a number (#6064).
  • Middle click mutes the volume or the microphone, or turns Do not disturb on or off; Shift + wheel on the volume switches the output device; the microphone's mute also turns its level to 0 (and back).
  • Volume and battery percentages, and the screen's brightness on the wheel with its own small panel (#6064).
  • The control center's item has its own icon; the control center's buttons can be on the pill, each on its own (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, night light, hotspot, airplane mode, project, cast, captions, accessibility, screenshot, lock, emoji, clipboard, Task Manager, Calculator, File Explorer), each with its own place in the order; the order's hint says items can be dragged (#6146).
  • New items: the keyboard's language and input mode (中/英), with a bubble when it changes while minimized (#6068); the apps using the microphone, camera or location (#6071); USB drives (open, eject, and a notice when one is plugged in) (#6071); virtual desktops (the wheel switches them); folders and places, browsed in Finder-like columns (#6065); wallpapers from a folder, with transitions.
  • An optional bubble with what's copied (#6064).

Calendar

  • Agendas (#6144): .ics links or files on a drive (Google Calendar's secret iCal address, Outlook and others; a Google Calendar page link is read as its iCal address), added from the calendar's gear or in the mod's settings, read only, repeating events too, each agenda in its own color; the next events under the month, with the year when it's another one.
  • Today's color: red, Windows' accent color or any color (#6144).

What's playing

  • The wheel on it can change the song instead of the volume (option); clicking the cover brings its app to the front; long titles and artists scroll in its panel under the mouse (#6146).
  • On the pill, the mouse over it shows the whole title and the artist, and a long title can keep scrolling while it plays (option).
  • The app's own volume and mute in its panel.

Notifications

  • A count and the app's name on unread apps' icons (WhatsApp's counts its unread messages); one icon per app for apps that send notifications under several IDs, like Phone Link's phone apps (option, on by default).
  • Clicking a notification also opens apps hidden in the tray, like QQ and WeChat (#6063).
  • Notifications that came while the island wasn't running (the PC off, the island turned off) and are still in Windows' list show on the island when it starts.
  • With the bar style, banners drop out of its middle; banners arriving while a panel is open wait for it to close.
  • The bell's right click opens the notifications with their switches; optional Win+N and Win+A open the island's notifications and control center instead of Windows' (#6064).
  • Snipping Tool's notifications can open the picture just saved in File Explorer instead of the app (option) (#6107).
  • Selecting text with the mouse in the pill's reply box.

Control center, power and weather

  • Wi-Fi: a switch to turn it on or off, connect, disconnect or forget a network (two clicks), the whole reason when connecting fails, and the cable's state and speed.
  • komorebi (if installed): start, stop and reload buttons with its version, as an optional button on the pill and as a control center section; each runs komorebi's own komorebic only on a click, without a window; when it fails, a visible terminal shows that attempt's output. Options for whkd and masir. Nothing is installed for the user, and the mod never stops komorebi by itself.
  • Power: the row says it's the Windows power plan (#6101).
  • Weather: cities found by their Chinese names when the island's texts are in Chinese (#6101).

Tray icons

  • Names in a bubble drawn like the island, with the program's name for icons that send none (#6065).
  • The icons not pinned can open in a list under the pill, as a grid or with their names, which stays open while an app's menu shows (#6065); the grid and the list say how to pin one.
  • Dragged with the mouse: reordered in the list, the grid and the list with names; pinned ones put anywhere on the pill, beside any item (they go with it, in every style and notch); from the list to the pill (pinned there) and back (unpinned). Each island keeps its own: the ones following the main settings share them, and a monitor with a profile of its own keeps them in it.
  • A click in the room between two icons goes to the nearer one (#6065); right clicks reach every app's menu, including Qt apps like VLC and qBittorrent.

Taskbar

  • New installs keep the Windows taskbar as it is (the dock is a choice in the settings).
  • "Hide the Windows taskbar's clock and tray" for the unchanged taskbar, and hiding the taskbar with every taskbar choice (#6048).
  • The transparent taskbar on the top and side edges, and a fix for the dock and the taskbar taking turns while the hidden taskbar slid.

Other

  • Chinese (Simplified) texts and settings.
  • Smoother and lighter: no stalls when opening panels, high-resolution frame pacing, scrolling texts moving smoothly, panels opening under the clicked item in every style, and options that are off run nothing (#6099); panels left open draw nothing while nothing happens: a text box's caret stops blinking after a few seconds, long names scroll only under the mouse, the settings aren't laid out again every 2 seconds, and an open panel isn't redrawn by the island's own animations, like the usage counts (#6151).

entry.title: Spotlight Launcher 0.5.11
entry.content:
Spotlight Launcher

A fast, keyboard-driven application launcher for Windows, packaged as a Windhawk tool mod.

Press Alt + Space, type a few letters, press Enter. That is the whole idea.

Spotlight Launcher indexes the same applications you see in the Start menu (classic programs and Microsoft Store / MSIX apps) and filters them as you type. It runs in its own windhawk.exe process, so it never gets injected into Explorer and cannot affect the shell.

Screenshots

Main

The search bar over the desktop, with the default Midnight colour and Acrylic effect. A short query already filtered a handful of results, with the matching letters highlighted. This is the launcher's first impression.

Details panel

An app selected with the details panel open on the right (Ctrl + I): the actions list and the technical info table.

Look and feel

These are some of the built-in looks (themes): the Aurora effect in three colours, plus Frosted, Glass and Mica.

| Theme | Preview | | --- | --- | | Aurora · Amber | | | Aurora · Emerald | | | Aurora · Violet | | | Frosted | | | Glass | | | Mica | |

The rest (the Acrylic and Solid effects and the remaining colours — Midnight blue, Graphite, Black, Teal, Rose, Crimson, Sky, Lavender, White) are covered below in the Features section.

Features

Instant, forgiving search

  • Filters classic programs and Microsoft Store apps as you type.
  • Case- and accent-insensitive.
  • Multi-word queries (visual code) and acronyms (vsc finds Visual Studio Code).
  • Matching letters are highlighted in the result.
  • Results show a friendly name plus the real target (exe, .lnk, MSIX package).

Keyboard-first

Everything is reachable without touching the mouse.

| Shortcut | Action | | --- | --- | | Alt + Space | Open / close the search bar (configurable) | | ↑ / ↓ / Tab | Move the selection | | Enter | Open the selected app | | Esc | Close the details panel, then the search bar | | Ctrl + Enter | Open the file location | | Ctrl + Shift + Enter | Run as administrator | | Ctrl + Shift + C | Copy the path | | Ctrl + P | Properties | | Ctrl + Shift + R | Remove from recents | | Ctrl + I | Toggle the details panel (configurable) | | Ctrl + R | Reindex the app list | | Mouse wheel | Scroll the list without changing the selection | | Mouse hover | Highlight the row under the cursor |

Alt + Space is also the system shortcut for a window's title-bar menu (Move, Size, Close…). While the mod is enabled with the default shortcut, that menu is not reachable by keyboard, so pick another combination in the settings if you use it. Apps like PowerToys Run make the same trade-off.

Details panel

Press Ctrl + I (or Ctrl + K / Ctrl + Space / F4) with an app selected to reveal a right-hand panel with actions and technical data. The actions also work with the panel closed. File actions are only offered for desktop apps; Store (MSIX) apps only expose open and remove from recents.

Appearance

  • Six background effects (Acrylic, Mica, Glass, Frosted, Aurora, Solid) and 12 colours.
  • Effects capture what is behind the bar on open, blur it and composite it inside the rounded card (tint, grain, highlights, gradients) — so they look the same on Windows 10 and 11 without undocumented DWM APIs.
  • Adjustable panel opacity, blur strength and layout.
  • Adapts to the DPI of each monitor.
  • The bar can sit anywhere from against the top edge to against the bottom edge of the screen.

Fresh without fuss

  • Automatic index updates watch the Start menu folders and re-read the list when an app is installed or removed, with a light periodic fallback for Store apps.
  • Can also re-index on every open or on a fixed interval (1 / 3 / 5 / 10 minutes).
  • Installers write an "Uninstall …" shortcut for everything they install; the mod inspects what each shortcut actually runs and hides the uninstallers and documentation, while keeping real tools whose names merely contain "uninstall".
  • If reindexing finishes with the search bar already open, the list updates by itself.
  • Only what Windows lists as an app appears: a portable program without a shortcut in the Start menu is not indexed. A freshly installed app may take a few seconds to appear, until Windows registers its shortcut.

Safe by design

  • Runs as a Windhawk tool mod in its own process, not inside Explorer.
  • Disable in fullscreen: the hotkey stays quiet while a fullscreen window (a game, a video player, a fullscreen browser) is focused.
  • If another app already owns the shortcut, the mod warns you instead of fighting over it.

Installation

  1. Install Windhawk (Windows 10 or 11).
  2. In Windhawk, open Mods and search for Spotlight Launcher, then click Install.
  3. Press Alt + Space to open it. Change the shortcut, position, effect and colour from the mod's Settings tab.

From source

  1. Download spotlight-launcher.wh.cpp.
  2. In Windhawk, choose Create a new mod, replace the editor contents with the file and Save.
  3. Install it from your local mods list.

Contributing

Contributions are welcome — bug reports, fixes, new features and translations alike. See the repository for details.

Reporting a bug

Open an issue and include:

  • Windows build (winver) and Windhawk version.
  • The mod version (shown in the README header / settings).
  • Steps to reproduce it and what you expected instead.
  • A screenshot or short clip when the problem is visual.

Sending a pull request

  1. Fork the repository and create a branch from main, e.g. fix/acrylic-on-win10.
  2. Make your change in spotlight-launcher.wh.cpp (C++23, Windhawk tool mod).
  3. Bump @version in the mod header when behaviour changes.
  4. Confirm it compiles and test it on the Windows versions you can reach.
  5. Open a pull request against main describing what changed and why.

Keep pull requests focused: one bug or feature per PR is much easier to review and merge.

License

entry.title: Win10 Taskbar Search State Refresh on Win11 24H2+ 1.0.0
entry.content:
Win10 Taskbar Search State Refresh

This mod addresses an issue where the legacy Windows 10 taskbar, running inside a Windows 11 system, does not always redraw when the taskbar Search setting (hidden / icon / box) is changed. It monitors the setting and triggers the taskbar to apply it immediately. This modification has been tested on Windows 11 24H2.

Note: for a complete Windows 10 taskbar experience on Windows 11 24H2 / 25H2, install the Windows 10 taskbar on Windows 11 24H2 mod first. That mod downloads and runs the Windows 10 explorer.exe (10.0.19039) as the shell; this mod only works on top of that shell and does nothing on the stock Windows 11 taskbar.

How it works

  • It monitors HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Search\SearchboxTaskbarMode (0 = hidden, 1 = icon, 2 = box, 3 = icon and label) via a registry notification, with a one-second poll as a fallback in case a notification is missed.
  • When the value changes, it sends WM_SETTINGCHANGE with "TraySettings" to Shell_TrayWnd and Shell_SecondaryTrayWnd of this process. This is the single method that reliably makes the Windows 10 taskbar reload its settings, including the search mode, on shell build 10.0.19039. The message is sent twice with a short gap so a momentarily busy explorer still catches it.
  • The message is never broadcast system-wide: only the taskbar windows of this process are targeted. No fake SPI_SETWORKAREA and no UI Automation are used.
  • The startup refresh is skipped on a normal explorer start (the taskbar reads the value itself when it is created) and only runs when the mod is enabled while the taskbar is already running.
  • Every refresh is written to the Windhawk log.

"Search icon and label" (approximation)

The Windows 10 taskbar only supports three states: hidden, icon, and box. "Search icon and label" (value 3) is a Windows 11 option that the Windows 10 taskbar does not implement, so by default selecting it changes nothing there. As the closest equivalent, this mod makes the taskbar interpret value 3 as 2 (search box). This applies only to reads performed inside explorer.exe: the registry value itself is never modified, and the Windows 11 Settings page continues to show the user's choice. It is an approximation, not a true "icon and label" layout. It can be disabled with labelAsBox.

Settings

  • labelAsBox: treat "Search icon and label" as the search box (see above).

Limitations

  • This mod never restarts explorer and never writes to the registry. The "icon and label" mapping is performed by adjusting the value as returned to explorer.exe (RegQueryValueExW / RegGetValueW); if the taskbar reads the value by other means, the mapping will not take effect.
  • The mod does nothing on the stock Windows 11 shell (build 22000+); it exits at load time.

entry.title: Explorer List Zebra Stripes 0.13.0
entry.content:
Explorer List Zebra Stripes

Adds alternating stripes to compact file-list items in Explorer, including Details and List views.

Colors

Supports #RRGGBB and dynamic system color names: accent, background, foreground, highlight, highlighttext, window, windowtext, buttonface, buttontext, hotlight, graytext.

accent uses the Windows DWM colorization color. background and foreground are theme-aware neutral colors (high-contrast aware); other system names use Win32 system colors.

Opacity is a percentage: 0 = invisible, 100 = fully opaque.

Mod was tested on Windows 11 24H2 & 26H2.

entry.title: Toast auto-dismiss 1.0
entry.content:
Toast auto-dismiss

Windows 11 toast banners usually disappear on their own in about five seconds, but reminders and notifications from some apps can stay on the screen until you deal with them.

The mod watches for toast banners and closes them after a configurable timeout (5 seconds by default). Closing works exactly like pressing the banner's own close (X) button: the notification is not lost, it stays in the notification center, and no app notification settings are changed.

While the mouse pointer is over a banner, the countdown is paused, so the banner's own buttons (reply, dismiss, and similar) remain clickable for as long as needed.

Windows has its own "Dismiss notifications after this amount of time" option (Settings > Accessibility > Visual effects, 5 seconds by default), but many toasts ignore it and stay on the screen until dismissed. The mod closes banners that ignore the system setting, and its timeout can also be shorter than the system's five seconds.

The mod runs in a dedicated Windhawk process (as a tool mod) and does not inject into other applications.

Settings

  • Timeout (seconds) - the maximum time a banner stays on screen. Default: 5, set to 0 to disable the mod. Use a smaller value to make banners disappear faster, or a larger value as a safety net for notifications that get stuck on the screen. The value is limited to 3600 seconds.
  • Pause while hovered - keep the banner while the pointer is over it. Default: on.

How it works

The banner is a regular window owned by the Windows shell. The mod finds it by size and position in the bottom right corner of a monitor and closes it through UI Automation - the same interface screen readers use to press buttons. No hooks are installed, and no system files or registry keys are modified.

Limitations

  • Banners are detected by their position in the bottom right corner of a monitor, so banners shown elsewhere are not closed. This includes banners moved to another corner or monitor (for example by the Notifications placement mod) and right-to-left languages, where banners appear in the bottom left corner.
  • Toasts that are meant to stay on the screen until handled, such as incoming call or alarm notifications, are closed by the timeout as well. Point at a banner to pause the countdown while it matters.

entry.title: Mond Desktop Clock 3.5
entry.content:
A universal desktop clock widget inspired by the Mond Rainmeter skin by HipHopium. It runs in a dedicated tool process, not in Explorer.

Differentiating Feature Set While many desk clock widgets offer customizable styles, Mond provides unparalleled granular control over every character. Unlike standard overlays, we allow for per-letter customization, letting you set unique colors and shadows for individual characters within the day, date, or time (e.g., coloring only the 'S' in September). This level of detail, combined with multi-row support and precise offset controls, makes Mond a highly flexible styling tool.

The clock shows the weekday, date, and time in three independently styled rows. Drag it to position it; enable position locking to prevent accidental movement.

Key Features & Advanced Customization:

  • Three Independent Rows: Display Weekday, Date, and Time in separate, independently configurable rows.
  • Granular Letter Control: Set individual colors and shadow offsets for every single character in the day, date, or time.
  • Advanced Typography: Full control over font families (Quicksand, Anurati, etc.), size, bold/italic styling, letter spacing, and per-row horizontal offsets.
  • Layout Flexibility: Select a "Main Heading" row to automatically reorder the display (e.g., Date on top, Weekday below).
  • Position Management: Drag-and-drop placement with saved positions shared across all monitors connected to your PC.

Styling & Fonts: Fonts must be installed in Windows. Missing fonts are silently substituted by Windows. We support advanced typography using:

  • Quicksand
  • Anurati

Coloring & Formatting:

  • Separate text and shadow colors are available for the overall row, but individual letter overrides take precedence.
  • Per-letter styles are indexed by 1-based character position from left to right (including spaces).
  • The date displays without a comma.
  • Colours accept #RRGGBB or #AARRGGBB; the alpha component in the latter form is ignored.

entry.title: Window Wobble 1.0.0
entry.content:
Window Wobble

KDE-style spring-physics window dragging. Grab a title bar and the window follows your cursor like jelly - the title bar keeps up, the body trails behind, and it settles with a wobble when you let go.

Hold Shift (configurable) while grabbing to move a window normally.

Licensed GPL-3.0-or-later: you are free to use, study, modify and share it, and any version you distribute must stay open under the same terms.

How this differs from the Wobbly Windows mod

Wobbly Windows does the same effect from inside dwm.exe, using private uDWM symbols. That is the better place to do it: the content stays live, and it can wobble on snapping and resizing too, not just dragging.

This mod does not touch dwm.exe. It runs in the application's own process and draws the effect on its own Direct3D overlay. Pick whichever trade you prefer:

Reasons to use this one

  • No changes to Windhawk's process inclusion list - it works once enabled
  • Nothing is injected into the compositor, so a fault here cannot take the desktop down with it; at worst one application is affected
  • No dependency on private, undocumented DWM symbols, so a Windows update changing uDWM internals cannot break it

Reasons to use the other one

  • Window content stays live; here it is a snapshot, so a playing video appears frozen for the length of the drag
  • It wobbles on snap and resize as well as drag
  • One copy in the compositor, rather than a small overlay per application

Questions, problems or ideas? Join the Discord (https://discord.gg/8wwfPxfMWA) or open an issue (https://github.com/heyjeay/window-wobble/issues).

How it works

In plain terms

  1. You press on a title bar, and the mod quietly takes a photograph of the whole window.
  2. The real window is made invisible. Not minimised, not moved - just not drawn. Its taskbar button stays exactly where it was.
  3. The photograph is pinned to an invisible grid, like a sheet of rubber, and shown in the window's place. The top edge of the sheet is stiff and keeps up with your cursor; further down it gets floppier. That is the whole trick - the body lags behind the title bar because the bottom of the sheet is softer than the top.
  4. All the while you are dragging, the mod is just moving that rubber sheet around and letting the springs do what springs do.
  5. When you let go, the real window is moved to where you dropped it while it is still invisible, then made visible again underneath the photograph. Only once it is safely back does the photograph disappear, so you never catch the swap happening.

Two things follow from this, and they are the reason for the bypass key. The window content is a photograph for as long as you hold it, so a playing video looks frozen. And because the mod is doing the dragging instead of Windows, Windows' own dragging features do not happen - see the section above.

Under the hood

A title-bar press is caught at DispatchMessage, with DefWindowProc as a backup and WM_SYSCOMMAND/SC_MOVE alongside for apps that draw their own title bars. The mod then runs its own move loop in place of the one Windows would start: the window is captured with PrintWindow(PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT), cloaked so it leaves composition entirely, and a spring mesh of that capture is drawn on a Direct3D 11 + DirectComposition overlay until you let go.

The mesh is two layers of springs: a control spring pulling each vertex back to its rest position, with the stiffness falling off down the rows, and springs between neighbouring vertices so the grid holds together instead of turning to taffy. On release the control springs are switched to a stiff, overdamped pair so it snaps back rather than ringing.

The drag runs on one persistent worker thread per process, never in the message pump: PrintWindow(PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT) renders through DWM and needs the window's own thread pumping, so doing it inline deadlocks against the very loop that invoked it.

Only top-level windows are touched, and only ones DWM will cloak. Anything else is handed back to Windows, which then runs its own move loop as usual.

What you give up during a wobble drag

The mod replaces Windows' move loop, so for the windows it animates these do not happen:

  • Aero Snap (dragging to a screen edge or the top)
  • the Snap Layouts bar at the top of the screen
  • restoring a snapped window's previous size when you drag it out
  • shake to minimize
  • WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE / WM_MOVING / WM_EXITSIZEMOVE, which docking UIs such as Visual Studio's tool windows use to show drop targets

Hold the bypass key (Shift by default) while grabbing to get all of that back for a drag.

Excluded processes

Shell and UI-host processes are excluded, since none of them own a window you would drag: sihost.exe, RuntimeBroker.exe, StartMenuExperienceHost.exe, ShellExperienceHost.exe, SearchHost.exe, TextInputHost.exe, ApplicationFrameHost.exe and NVDisplay.Container.exe.

Windhawk never injects into the critical system processes (csrss.exe, dwm.exe, lsass.exe and the rest), so those need no entry here.

Notes

Window content is a snapshot for the duration of the drag, so a playing video appears frozen while you hold it. This is inherent to the approach - capturing live content per frame is far more expensive than one PrintWindow.

The Direct3D device and the overlay are released after a few seconds without a drag, so an application you dragged once does not hold them for the rest of its life. They are rebuilt on the next drag, which costs a few milliseconds.

entry.title: Excel Wheel Sheet Navigation 0.5.4
entry.content:
Excel Wheel Sheet Navigation

For 64-bit desktop Excel on Windows:

  • Vertical wheel over the bottom sheet tabs scrolls the tab strip without changing the active sheet.
  • Horizontal wheel over the worksheet or sheet tabs activates the adjacent visible sheet.
  • The tab strip uses Excel's native navigation arrows and animation. If the arrows cannot be used, it falls back to ScrollWorkbookTabs.
  • Repeated same-direction horizontal wheel messages are grouped with a 200 ms quiet period by default; the first switch is immediate.
  • Hidden sheets are skipped. Modified wheel input and ordinary vertical worksheet scrolling keep Excel's behavior.

Settings allow direct sheet activation instead of tab scrolling, reversing direction, disabling horizontal switching, and optional wraparound. No macros are required. Activating a sheet can trigger existing workbook activation events, just like clicking a tab. Tested on one installation of 64-bit Microsoft 365 Excel; other Office versions and 32-bit Excel have not been tested.

Excel 滚轮切换工作表

默认操作：标签栏上下滚轮平滑滚动标签；点击标签切换工作表。 单元格区域左右滚轮切换到相邻的可见工作表。

标签栏滚动使用左下角左右箭头的原生操作路径和动画， 不再使用图像覆盖或淡入淡出。滚动不改变当前工作表。 左右拨动产生的连续同方向信号会合并，一次拨动只切换一张。

将鼠标放到 Excel 底部的工作表标签上，根据“滚轮行为”选择：

  • 直接切换工作表：向下切换到下一张可见工作表，向上切换到上一张。 隐藏的工作表会跳过。
  • 只滚动标签栏：向下显示右侧标签，向上显示左侧标签；当前工作表保持不变， 找到目标标签后点击进入。

单元格区域的上下滚轮仍然滚动表格内容。左右滚轮切换可以单独关闭， 关闭后恢复 Excel 原来的横向滚动。水平滚动条、状态栏或功能区保留原有行为。 单元格编辑、查找对话框或其他窗口占用焦点时不进行切换。

只适用于 Windows 桌面版 64 位 Excel。通过 Excel 自身的工作表对象切换， 不需要启用宏，也不会更改工作簿中的数据。切换工作表会触发工作簿自身已有 的工作表激活事件，与手动点击标签一样。

左右拨动防重复默认 200 毫秒：同方向连续信号合并为一次拨动， 停顿后再次切换，反方向立即切换。标签栏直接切换模式的间隔仍为 150 毫秒。

entry.title: App Owned Frame 1.44
entry.content:
App Owned Frame

Some applications draw their own title bar. With the Windows classic theme, they can show an extra white border or a second system title bar. When maximized, their hidden frame edges can also become visible on the neighbouring monitor.

This mod keeps the application's own frame and restores normal maximized-window clipping. It does not remove resizable-window styles, replace the application's buttons, change the client layout or run its own resize loop.

Requirements

  • Windows 11, build 22000 or later, and Windhawk 1.7.3 or later.
  • An already enabled classic theme, for example Classic Theme or Classic Theme Enable with extended compatibility. This mod is a compatibility fix, not a classic-theme enabler.

Default application profiles

| Application | Default treatment | | --- | --- | | Discord | Remove the extra white frame; use the normal resize cursor with wider grips. | | ChatGPT and Claude | Fix the outer frame and maximized clipping without loading this mod into the app. | | Photoshop | Keep its own title bar and prepare it during startup. | | DaVinci Resolve | Keep its own title bar and colour a remaining resize gutter to match the dark UI. |

These profiles were tested on the submitter's setup. App updates, Windows versions and other frame/DPI mods can affect the result.

The dedicated helper and the in-process application hooks share one mod source. Windhawk 1.7.3 is the runtime tested on this setup; Windhawk 2.0 alpha has not yet been runtime-tested with this combined configuration.

Adding or excluding an application

  1. Open this mod's Settings tab and add the executable filename or full path under Applications with their own frame. Wildcards * and ? are supported.
  2. Leave Frame geometry on Automatic initially. Use Off to exclude an entry without deleting it. Only main resizable windows with an app-drawn title bar are handled; ordinary Windows captions, dialogs and tool windows are skipped.
  3. For an extra classic title bar like Photoshop or Resolve, enable Use the application's own title bar. Open this mod's Advanced tab, add the executable to the Custom process inclusion list, and save.
  4. For Chromium/Electron apps, Native resize hit testing is optional and also requires that Advanced inclusion entry. Enable it only after testing the app. Discord is included by default. Do not add Claude or ChatGPT to that list merely to fix their border; their default profiles intentionally stay external.

The application list chooses which windows to treat. The Advanced inclusion list is needed only for features which load code into the application. When an enabled feature needs different hooks, saving settings reloads this mod in that process. Changing the grip size or colour does not require an app restart.

Easier resizing

Easier resizing from all corners and edges widens the grab areas without drawing a frame. All four corners use the same size; edges use half that size. The size is in pixels at 100% scale and is adjusted for the window's monitor.

Discord's native mode provides the usual hover resize cursor. For external-only apps the cursor changes when the drag starts, not while hovering. Larger grips extend into the window and can overlap the edge of a scrollbar or caption button; reduce the size or disable wider grips if this makes an app control hard to click.

Other options and limitations

  • Residual resize gutter color paints only the remaining frame gutter, not client content. Resolve defaults to #17181a; leave it empty to disable.
  • Prepare the custom title bar at startup is enabled for Photoshop. Other apps must opt in after testing. It takes priority over the experimental Delegate caption painting to DWM option.
  • Remove system backdrop from the frame is for a remaining bright material edge and requires Windows 11 build 22621 or later.
  • The external correction runs in a dedicated Windhawk process, not Explorer. A clean disable restores captured values. Scalar rollback data stays on each window if that helper crashes; reloading the mod recovers it after validating the application and former helper process identities. Unreadable original border/caption colours return to the system default.
  • This does not fix unrelated application rendering bugs, DPI-projection bugs or conflicts with another mod which keeps rewriting the same frame state. No application/system light or dark setting is changed.

entry.title: Cursor Idle Fade 1.0.0
entry.content:
Cursor Idle Fade

When the mouse hasn't moved (or been clicked / scrolled) for the configured number of seconds, the system cursors are smoothly faded out. The moment any mouse activity happens, the cursors are restored immediately.

How it works

Windows has no "cursor opacity" setting, so the mod captures the current system cursors, then swaps them for progressively more transparent copies using SetSystemCursor. Mouse activity (movement, clicks and scrolling) is detected with raw input, so nothing is polled while the cursor is visible. While the cursor is faded, a slow watchdog (every 250 ms, or every 50 ms while an elevated app has focus, see Limitations) also checks the mouse and the input desktop. On activity the original cursors are put back with SetSystemCursor (which updates the cursor on screen immediately), followed by a reload of the saved cursor scheme with SPI_SETCURSORS, so the scheme's own cursors are in place again.

The mod runs in its own dedicated windhawk.exe process (a Windhawk "tool mod").

How this differs from similar mods

  • Cursor auto-hide on idle hides the cursor outright once the idle delay has passed and shows it again on the first movement or click. This mod fades the cursor out gradually instead of making it vanish abruptly:

  • The fade is smooth (eased) and its length is a setting. A fade duration of 0 hides the cursor instantly, like a plain auto-hide.

  • The final opacity is a setting too, so the cursor can fade to, say, 20% and stay findable instead of disappearing completely.

    If you just want the cursor gone after a delay, that mod is the simpler choice. This one is for people who prefer a soft fade, or want the cursor dimmed rather than hidden.

    Both mods swap the same system cursors and reload the cursor scheme when they restore, so they aren't meant to be enabled together. Pick one.

Limitations

  • Only the standard system cursors are faded (arrow, I-beam, hand, resize, cross, help, etc.). Apps that draw their own cursor (some games, some browsers/design tools) are not affected.
  • The animated busy/working cursors are left alone on purpose.
  • Monochrome cursors can't be made partially transparent. With the default Windows cursor scheme this includes the text (I-beam) and precision (crosshair) cursors. They stay unchanged until the fade passes 50% and then disappear; if Final opacity is 50 or more, they stay visible.
  • The faded copies are single-size bitmaps. With mixed-DPI monitors or a larger pointer size, the cursor may change size while it fades and snap back when restored.
  • Restoring reloads your saved cursor scheme, so cursors changed temporarily by another tool via SetSystemCursor revert to the saved scheme.
  • Windows doesn't deliver raw mouse input to a normal (non-elevated) process while an app running as administrator has focus (Task Manager, for example). In that case the mod falls back to checking the cursor position and mouse buttons (about 5 times a second): the cursor still reappears when you move or click, but scrolling alone isn't noticed. The mod notices which app has focus and switches back to raw input by itself.
  • If the cursor is faded while a secure screen (UAC prompt, lock screen) takes the input, it is restored automatically.

Recovery

If the mod's process crashes while the cursor is faded, it tries to restore the cursors before it exits. If the process is killed instead, the mod restores the cursors the next time it starts. You can also re-apply your cursor scheme in Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Mouse > Additional mouse settings > Pointers.

entry.title: Taskbar Spatial Order 1.0
entry.content:
Taskbar Spatial Order

Keeps each app's windows on the taskbar in the order they sit on your screens, left to right, then top to bottom, rather than roughly the order they were opened. Hover over an app's taskbar button and its leftmost window is the leftmost thumbnail; uncombined buttons follow the same order.

Without the mod, the previews follow the order the windows were opened:

With it, they follow the windows on screen:

The order follows as windows move, are minimised or restored, open or close. The mod waits until things have been still for a moment, and while a window is dragged or the Start menu, search, notifications or a jump list is open.

By default, minimised windows go last and a group whose windows are all minimised is left alone. The settings can change both and exclude apps.

Limitations

  • Windows 11 24H2 and later, with its own taskbar, tested on build 26300; older versions are untested. The mod relies on internal taskbar functions found through Windows debug symbols, which an update can change; if one is missing or looks unexpected, the mod logs it and does nothing.
  • A button that moves is taken off the taskbar and put back, which can show as a brief animation. Only buttons that are out of place move, and they keep their progress bar, overlay badge and thumbnail toolbar buttons.
  • The mod's order wins: a window moved to another place in its group, by hand or by another mod, goes back at the next sort.

Credits

The move-and-refresh technique and the code that finds the taskbar's lists are adapted from Taskbar Thumbnail Reorder by m417z, with a smaller part from his Cycle taskbar buttons with mouse wheel mod.
